item.title: OPEC+ meets as oil tops $109 amid Iran war supply crisis
item.description:
Crude oil prices ended the week at their highest sustained levels in years, with Brent crude settling near $109 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate at roughly $112 on Friday, as the five-week-old U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran continues to choke off a substantial share of the world's energy supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

The conflict, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, was launched on February 28 at the direction of President Donald Trump. Iran responded by imposing what amounts to a selective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz beginning March 15, operating a permission-based transit route that has reduced tanker traffic to a trickle. Crude and condensate loadings from the Persian Gulf plunged to 4.3 million barrels per day in March, down from 16.6 million in February, according to maritime intelligence firm Windward. The International Energy Agency has called it the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market".

item.title: Zelenskyy warns prolonged Iran war is eroding US support for Ukraine
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he fears a prolonged U.S.-Israeli war against Iran will steadily drain American support for Ukraine, warning in an exclusive Associated Press interview late Saturday in Istanbul that "we have to recognize that we are not the priority for today".

Speaking as the Middle East conflict enters its sixth week, Zelenskyy told the AP that deliveries of critically needed U.S.-made Patriot air defense missiles — essential for intercepting Russian ballistic strikes on Ukrainian cities — are already shrinking and will only get worse. "The package — which is not very big for us — I think will be smaller and smaller day by day," he said.

item.title: Gulf nations mobilize to secure food as Iran war chokes imports
item.description: Governments across the Gulf and broader Middle East are accelerating efforts to safeguard food supplies as the war involving Iran continues to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint that handles over 70% of food imports into the Gulf Cooperation Council countries. In the past week, the UAE, Qatar, and Jordan have each unveiled measures ranging from border inspections to emergency financing packages aimed at keeping shelves stocked and prices stable.

item.title: U.S. destroyed own aircraft in Iran during rescue of downed F-15E crew member
item.description: Two U.S. Air Force MC-130J Commando II special operations aircraft were deliberately destroyed by American forces inside Iran after becoming stuck at a remote improvised airstrip during a rescue mission to extract a downed F-15E crew member, U.S. officials confirmed on Saturday. The destruction, ordered by field commanders, was carried out to prevent sensitive equipment from falling into Iranian hands as the dramatic operation unfolded in the mountains of southwestern Iran.

item.title: Israeli drone strike kills 4 in Gaza City amid fragile ceasefire
item.description:
An Israeli drone strike killed four Palestinians and wounded several others in Gaza City before dawn on Sunday, according to Gaza's civil defense agency and Al-Shifa Hospital, in the latest violence to overshadow a nearly six-month-old ceasefire.

The civil defense agency said the strike hit a group of civilians in an eastern neighborhood of Gaza City, while medics cited by Reuters said the airstrike targeted people on Jaffa Street near the Darraj neighborhood. Al-Shifa Hospital confirmed the toll, reporting that "four martyrs and five wounded arrived at the hospital this morning after an Israeli drone fired two missiles at a group of civilians". The Israeli military said it was looking into the reports.

item.title: Iran war oil shock fuels stagflation warnings worldwide
item.description: The escalating U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran has choked off oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, sending crude prices well above $100 per barrel and forcing central banks and economists worldwide to confront the prospect of a prolonged inflation surge — or worse, stagflation.

item.title: US, Israel strike Iranian air defenses and energy sites as Gulf attacks intensify
item.description: Joint US-Israeli forces struck an S-300 surface-to-air missile defense site near Tehran and multiple petrochemical facilities in Iran's Khuzestan Province on Saturday, April 4, as the conflict that began on February 28 entered its 37th day with no diplomatic resolution in sight. Iran responded with its heaviest single-day barrage against the United Arab Emirates, which intercepted 23 ballistic missiles and 56 drones, while falling debris caused fires and damage across the Gulf state.

item.title: Saudi Arabia deploys first Arab satellite on Artemis II mission
item.description:
Saudi Arabia on Saturday confirmed the successful deployment and initial communication with its Shams satellite, carried aboard NASA's Space Launch System rocket as part of the Artemis II mission. The milestone makes Saudi Arabia the first Arab nation to participate in a mission under NASA's Artemis program.

The Shams CubeSat, developed domestically by Saudi teams, was released from the SLS rocket after the Orion crew capsule separated and began its journey toward the Moon. The Saudi Space Agency confirmed communication with the satellite, which is now operating in a highly elliptical orbit ranging from approximately 500 to 70,000 kilometers above Earth.

item.title: Artemis II crew spots lunar features never seen by human eyes
item.description: Four days into humanity's first voyage to the Moon in more than half a century, NASA's Artemis II crew has sent back a trove of images that are already reshaping how scientists and the public see Earth and its nearest celestial neighbor. Among them: the first-ever full view of the Moon's Orientale Basin seen by human eyes, early glimpses of the lunar far side, and a portrait of Earth that has drawn instant comparisons to the iconic "Blue Marble" photograph from Apollo 17.

item.title: Artemis II crew sees far side of the Moon
item.description: The convergence of a blockbuster space film and NASA's first crewed lunar mission in over half a century has created a rare moment of shared excitement around space exploration. Project Hail Mary, the Ryan Gosling-led sci-fi adventure, has dominated the box office since its March 20 release, while NASA's Artemis II mission — carrying four astronauts on a flyby around the Moon — launched on April 1 and is now en route back to Earth.

item.title: Navy SEALs rescue downed F-15E airman from Iran
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced early Sunday that U.S. Special Operations forces had successfully rescued the second crew member from an F-15E Strike Eagle shot down over Iran, capping a two-day operation that military officials called one of the most challenging in U.S. special operations history.

"WE GOT HIM!" Trump wrote on Truth Social, describing the rescued airman as a "brave Warrior" who had been "behind enemy lines in the treacherous mountains of Iran, being hunted down by our enemies, who were getting closer and closer by the hour."

item.title: Trump's 48-hour Iran ultimatum expires Monday as strikes hit Mahshahr
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his confrontation with Iran on Saturday, warning Tehran it has 48 hours to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating military consequences, as U.S. and Israeli forces struck Iran's largest petrochemical complex and ceasefire talks collapsed.

"Remember when I gave Iran ten days to MAKE A DEAL or OPEN UP THE HORMUZ STRAIT," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Saturday morning. "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!" The ultimatum sets a Monday, April 6, deadline that Trump has repeatedly extended since first threatening to destroy Iran's power plants on March 21.

item.title: US has lost at least 7 aircraft in Iran war, CNN reports
item.description: The United States Air Force has lost at least seven manned aircraft since the start of its war with Iran, CNN reported on Saturday, a tally that undercuts the Trump administration's repeated assertions of near-total air dominance over the country.

item.title: Israel halted strikes, shared intel to aid US airman rescue in Iran
item.description: Israel provided critical intelligence support and suspended its own airstrikes to help the United States rescue a downed F-15E crew member stranded deep inside Iran, an Israeli military official confirmed on Sunday. The disclosure sheds new light on the close coordination between the two allies during one of the most dramatic military operations of the five-week-old war.

item.title: Pope Leo celebrates first Easter with call to 'lay down' weapons
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV marked his first Easter as leader of the Catholic Church on Sunday, celebrating Mass before some 50,000 people in a sun-drenched St. Peter's Square before delivering a pointed appeal for world leaders to choose peace over conflict.

"Let those who have weapons lay them down!" the pope declared from the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica in his Urbi et Orbi message — the traditional Easter address "to the city and the world." "Let those who have the power to unleash wars choose peace — not a peace imposed by force, but through dialogue, not with the desire to dominate others, but to encounter them!"

item.title: Iran's internet blackout is now longest on record at 37 days
item.description:
Iran's nationwide internet shutdown has become the longest government-imposed blackout ever recorded in any country, entering its 37th consecutive day on Saturday after 864 hours of near-total disconnection, according to global internet monitor NetBlocks.

"Iran's internet blackout is now the longest nation-scale internet shutdown on record in any country, exceeding all other comparable incidents in severity," NetBlocks said in a post on X on April 5. The organization noted that while some countries have experienced intermittent or regional shutdowns over longer periods, no nation had previously imposed a continuous nationwide blackout of this duration.

item.title: Durov vows Telegram will evade Russia's ban, cites Iran parallels
item.description:
Telegram co-founder Pavel Durov said on Saturday that approximately 50 million Iranians continue to use the messaging app through VPNs despite a years-long government ban, calling them "50 million members of the Digital Resistance in Iran." The remarks came as part of a broader post in which Durov also addressed Russia's recent decision to block Telegram, drawing a direct parallel between the two countries' failed censorship strategies.

"Iran banned Telegram years ago, with a result similar to Russia," Durov wrote on his Telegram channel. "The government hoped for mass adoption of its surveillance messaging apps, but instead VPN usage exploded." He added that "the whole nation is mobilized to circumvent these absurd restrictions" and pledged that Telegram would adapt its traffic to become harder to detect and block.

item.title: Iran detains dissidents' families, seizes property to silence exiled opposition
item.description: Iran's government is detaining the family members of opposition figures living in exile and threatening to seize their property, according to reports gathered by The Associated Press, in what dissidents describe as a widening crackdown on dissenting voices as the country remains engulfed in conflict.

item.title: Indonesia receives slain UN peacekeepers as UNIFIL threats mount
item.description:
Indonesia on Saturday received the remains of three United Nations peacekeepers killed during Israel's military operations in southern Lebanon, as mounting attacks on UN personnel drew international condemnation.

The coffins of the fallen soldiers, draped in the Indonesian flag, arrived at Jakarta's international airport and were carried into a ceremonial hall by uniformed comrades in a solemn ceremony attended by President Prabowo Subianto.

item.title: Israeli airstrike kills displaced family in southern Lebanon
item.description:
Israeli airstrikes killed a displaced family in the southern Lebanese town of Kfar Hatta on Sunday, as the military intensified its aerial campaign across the country and warned it would strike near the main Syria-Lebanon border crossing.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported six members of one family were killed in the strike on Kfar Hatta, a town from which the Israeli military had earlier ordered evacuations. The family had been displaced from Kfar Tibnit in the Nabatieh district and was sheltering in the town when the attack occurred. A Lebanese civil defense source told AFP the family had been waiting for a relative to pick them up so they could leave. At least three more people were killed in a separate airstrike elsewhere in southern Lebanon on Sunday morning.
